title: Collaterals Agent
text:
Collaterals Agent
Project: Collaterals Agent (Simplilearn, Jun – Aug 2025)
An N8N-based multi-agent system that cut course-launch marketing collateral from 7–10 days to 1 day.
Problem
Every new course launch needed SD/SL pages, brochures and seven types of emailers. Two teams of four people (eight in total) spent 7–10 days producing them.

title: Collaterals Agent
text:
Collaterals Agent
What Rishabh built
- An N8N-based agentic system that drafts all collateral automatically and cuts turnaround to one day, including reviews and approvals.
- A fine-tuned GPT model with deep course knowledge drafts accurate, relevant marketing content.
- Architecture: one Head Agent coordinates two sub-agents:
  - a Researcher, which gathers and validates course information through SerpAPI;
  - an Analyst, which checks content structure and data accuracy and extracts the table of contents.
- Integrated with Google Docs for automatic document creation and real-time updates throughout the workflow.

Outcome

title: AI-Powered Osteoarthritis Classification & Reporting
text:
AI-Powered Osteoarthritis Classification & Reporting
Project: AI-Powered Osteoarthritis Classification & Reporting (OsteosConnect, Jan 2024 – Sep 2024)
End-to-end knee X-ray grading on AWS — 96% accuracy, more than 90% concordance with radiologists, ahead of competitor RBKnee.
What it does
Doctors capture a knee X-ray on a React web app or an Android app. The system grades osteoarthritis automatically and produces a web-based report.

How it works
- Flow: capture on React/Android → encrypted upload to S3 → Lambda trigger → SageMaker/EC2 inference → prediction → Lambda → report written to the EMR.
- A closed feedback loop retrains the model on doctor-validated labels, so it keeps improving with real clinical use.
- Earlier, as an intern, Rishabh ran EDA on DICOM images and built baseline classifiers (logistic regression, random forest) before moving to deep learning.

text:
How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
Blog post: How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0) (31 Oct 2026)
A Python LangGraph agent, hybrid RAG with FAISS + BM25 and re-ranking, free LLMs with fallbacks, and RAGAS evals.
Recruiters rarely have time to read a whole portfolio, so I put an agent on this site that answers questions about my work. Here's how it's built.

The graph
The agent is a small LangGraph graph written in Python:

title: How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
text:
How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
The graph
The agent is a small LangGraph graph written in Python:

1. route: simple messages (hi, "how do I contact him?", prompt-injection attempts) get an instant reply without calling an LLM. That saves the free quota for real questions.
2. retrieve: hybrid search over this site's own content.
   - FAISS finds chunks with similar meaning, using Gemini embeddings.
   - BM25 finds exact keywords.
   - Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges the two rankings.
3. rerank: a cross-encoder (bge-reranker-base) reads the question and each chunk together, and keeps the best 4.
4. respond: an LLM answers from those chunks only, and streams the reply token by token.

title: How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
text:
How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
Free models, with fallbacks
Free LLM tiers have rate limits, so one provider is never enough. The agent tries Groq gpt-oss-120b first, then Gemini Flash-Lite, then more Groq and Gemini models, then free models on OpenRouter. The backend tracks every model's requests and tokens against its free limits, skips a model before it runs out, and trims older turns if a long conversation doesn't fit — so the switch is invisible. Only when every free model is used up does the chat pause, until the limits reset.

Security in front, AI behind
- The browser never talks to the Python agent directly.
- A Next.js gateway checks for bots, validates input, rate-limits each visitor and enforces a daily budget.
- Only then does it call the agent, using a shared secret.

title: How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
text:
How the AI agent on this site works (and why it costs ₹0)
Memory that disappears
Chat history lives only in your open browser tab. When you close the chat or leave the site, it's gone. All I keep is a short AI-written summary, plus your details only if you chose to share them.

Measuring it
- An eval suite checks that retrieval finds the right page, that answers contain the right facts, and that guardrails hold: no phone numbers, no leaked prompt, no invented claims.
- RAGAS scores faithfulness, answer relevancy and context precision, using a free model as the judge.
